Valve's Steam Frame headset gets a November release date

Published 2026-10-07 12:20 UTC

Valve says its Steam Frame standalone VR headset will ship on November 12th, starting at $599 for the 256GB model and $799 for 1TB. The headset runs SteamOS on an Arm chip and can stream PC games wirelessly from a gaming PC using a bundled dongle.

Valve is also opening preorders for the Steam Controller, which shares the headset's thumbsticks and trackpad layout. Developers have had access to dev kits since the summer, and Valve says more than 2,000 games are already verified to run well on the headset.

The launch puts Valve in direct competition with Meta's Quest headsets during the holiday season, though Valve is positioning the Frame as an extension of a gaming PC rather than a standalone console.

The Steam Frame has a pair of high-resolution LCD panels with pancake lenses, which make the headset thinner and lighter than earlier designs. Valve says it weighs about 440 grams with the strap and battery. Eye tracking is built in and used for foveated rendering, which focuses detail where the wearer is looking to save processing power.

Hands-on reports from developers describe sharp visuals and comfortable fit for long sessions, though battery life is about two and a half hours in standalone mode. Valve sells a separate battery pack that clips to the back of the strap for longer play.

Standalone games run on the headset's own chip, while more demanding titles stream from a gaming PC. Valve says the wireless dongle uses a dedicated connection to keep latency low, avoiding interference from household Wi-Fi networks. The headset can also run the SteamOS desktop for flat games on a large virtual screen.

Valve has not said how many units it expects to sell, but the company says production has been ramping since the summer to avoid shortages like those that followed the launch of its handheld gaming PC. Preorders will be fulfilled in the order they are placed, and Valve says most buyers should receive their headsets by the end of the year.
